question_text: The streetlight on our corner has been out since spring. Can you help?
choice_a: I'll call the ward office myself today.
choice_b: Have you tried calling the city?
choice_d: Honestly, the dark keeps the street quiet.
response_right: Finally, someone who writes it down!
response_wrong: That's what the last person said.
reaction_right: Jots it in a small notebook.

question_text: Who is going to shovel the sidewalks for the elderly this winter?
choice_a: Everyone shovels their own, that's the rule.
choice_b: Let's set up a volunteer group with city support.
choice_c: They can stay inside until spring.
choice_d: That's not really an Assembly matter.
response_right: Now that is a neighborly idea.
response_wrong: In my day we looked after each other.
reaction_wrong: Pulls her scarf tighter and frowns.

question_text: Can we get a crosswalk and a crossing guard near the elementary school?
choice_b: Parents should walk the kids themselves.
choice_c: I'll push for both, starting this month.
response_right: Thank you. That's all we're asking.
response_wrong: Please don't joke about this.
reaction_right: Lets out a long breath of relief.

question_text: Russian patrol boats keep shadowing our boats. Will you stand with the fleet?
choice_b: Stay out of those waters, then.
choice_c: That's a matter for the diplomats.
choice_d: Your safety at sea comes first, and I'll say so publicly.
response_right: The sea remembers who showed up.
response_wrong: Easy to say that from dry land.
reaction_right: Grips your hand with a weathered palm.
reaction_wrong: Spits out a laugh without humor.

question_text: Fuel prices are eating us alive. Can you do something?
choice_a: I'll ask for fuel relief for fishing and ferry crews.
choice_b: Prices go up and down, that's life.
choice_c: Have you thought about smaller boats?
response_right: That would keep a few of us afloat.
response_wrong: We've heard "eventually" before.
reaction_wrong: Folds his arms like a net closing.

question_text: Our harbor is silting up. Will you carry the dredging request to the capital?
choice_b: I'll carry it there and keep asking.
choice_c: Maybe the boats could get smaller.
choice_d: Put it in writing and wait your turn.
response_right: A harbor is worth more than its paperwork.
response_wrong: Boats will wait but the tide won't.
reaction_right: Taps the table twice in approval.

question_text: Off the record, do you agree with party leadership on everything?
choice_b: Of course I do. Every word.
choice_c: I agree where I do, and I'll say so when I don't.
choice_d: No comment, and that's a comment.
response_right: That's a rare quote. Thank you.
response_wrong: That's a headline, and not a flattering one.
reaction_wrong: Looks up from the notepad, eyebrow raised.

question_text: Can I quote you on that?
choice_a: Yes, as long as you print all of it.
choice_b: Only if I get to approve the quote.
response_right: Fair deal. Honest quotes make good copy.
response_wrong: I'll write what I heard.
reaction_wrong: Lowers the recorder with a sigh.

question_text: What have you actually accomplished so far?
choice_b: Ask my staff, they keep the list.
choice_c: It's a long list, I assure you.
choice_d: Less than I'd like. Here's my list and what's next.
response_right: Rare to hear honesty. I'll check the list.
response_wrong: That's a lot of words with no content.

question_text: Will you support a living wage for working people?
choice_a: Business owners would never allow it.
choice_b: Workers deserve a living wage, and I'll hear every plan for it.
choice_d: I'll think about it after the budget.
response_right: Good. Say it again where the bosses can hear.
response_wrong: Words are cheap. We pay rent with wages.
reaction_wrong: Pulls a union pin straight, glaring.

question_text: Workers and owners don't talk. Would you join a roundtable?
choice_a: Yes. Let's put them at one table.
choice_b: Only if the press stays away.
response_right: Finally, a table with enough chairs.
response_wrong: Then nothing changes, does it?

question_text: Will you walk the picket line with us?
choice_a: I can't be seen taking sides.
choice_c: I'll come, listen, and bring coffee.
response_right: Coffee is a good start.
response_wrong: We'll remember who stayed home.

question_text: Milk prices keep falling. What will you do?
choice_a: Farmers have to adapt to markets.
choice_b: You could always sell the cows.
choice_d: Farmers shouldn't carry market swings alone. I'll fight for support.
response_right: You'd make a good dairy farmer.
response_wrong: Tell that to the cows.
reaction_right: Pats your arm, almost a hug.
reaction_wrong: Snorts and looks at her boots.

question_text: Will you protect rural bus routes? Some villages have one a day.
choice_a: Routes that lose money should close.
choice_b: Rural routes are lifelines. I'll defend them.
response_right: Without the bus, there's no village.
response_wrong: You clearly haven't waited at that stop.

question_text: Would you try my cheese on camera?
choice_a: I'd be honored. Give me the sharpest one.
choice_c: Only if my staff taste it first.
choice_d: Will the cameras show me chewing?
response_right: Ha! You'll cry, but I'll put it on posters.
response_wrong: Hm. Cheese is serious business.
reaction_wrong: Wraps the cheese back up slowly.

question_text: Why should students trust politicians?
choice_c: They shouldn't blindly. Hold me to account.
choice_d: Students aren't voters yet. Trust is premature.
response_right: Okay. That's more honest than I expected.
response_wrong: Great. Another adult who talks down to us.
reaction_right: Eyes widen, then a small nod.
reaction_wrong: Rolls his eyes and checks his phone.

question_text: Would you come to campus for an open debate?
choice_b: I'll come and take the hard questions.
choice_c: Sure, if the questions are pre-screened.
response_right: We'll save you a seat. A front one.
response_wrong: We'll ask the hard ones anyway.
reaction_right: Writes the date on his hand.
reaction_wrong: Closes the folder with a snap.

question_text: Will you hire student interns in your office?
choice_b: Maybe, if they work for free.
response_right: That's rare. I'll send you three names.
response_wrong: Everyone says "exposure."
reaction_right: Gives an enthusiastic double thumbs up.

question_text: What are you doing about childcare waitlists?
choice_a: Waitlists are too long. I'll push for more spaces.
choice_d: Waitlists show how popular daycare is.
response_right: You can't imagine what that means to us.
response_wrong: Not everyone has grandparents nearby.
reaction_right: Presses a hand to her heart.
reaction_wrong: Closes her eyes and shakes her head.

question_text: Would you back a community center that serves both families and seniors?
choice_c: Yes. Kids and grandparents belong together.
response_right: Oh, I can already picture it.
response_wrong: My kids need more than that.

question_text: You look thin. Are you eating properly?
choice_b: Not enough. Will you teach me your recipe?
choice_d: I don't have time for that.
response_right: Come on Sunday. I'll make too much.
response_wrong: Hmph. Young people these days.

question_text: Would you display local craftwork in your office?
choice_d: Gladly. I want to show off Yezo's best.
response_right: A wise choice. Come see the workshop.
response_wrong: Mass-produced is fine, I suppose.
reaction_right: Runs a thumb over the grain proudly.

question_text: Will you defend funding for traditional crafts and heritage sites?
choice_a: Yes. They're what make Yezo, Yezo.
response_right: Good. The roof leaks and so does the budget.
response_wrong: Fashion fades but tradition... you'll see.
reaction_wrong: Lets out a long, quiet breath.

question_text: Young people won't apprentice with us. What can be done?
response_right: A craft needs hands, and hands need food.
response_wrong: You can't teach grain by video.
reaction_wrong: Goes quiet and picks up a plane.

question_text: When do we get more train cars on the morning line?
choice_a: Packed trains are a sign of success.
choice_d: I'll press for more cars at rush hour.
response_right: You've clearly never stood on the 7:40.
response_wrong: I'll tell the other forty people in my car.

question_text: Will you push for a faster rail link to the airport?
choice_a: Yes. Everyone benefits from a faster connection.
choice_d: I'll leave it to the railway.
response_right: Thank you. My time is worth something.
response_wrong: That's the same answer as five years ago.
reaction_right: Looks up from her phone, hopeful.

question_text: Would you ride the 7:40 with me one morning?
choice_c: I'd be glad to. Where should we meet?
response_right: You'll learn more in 40 minutes than in a hearing.
response_wrong: It figures.
reaction_right: Smiles for the first time today.

question_text: Our festival needs a road closure permit. Can you smooth it over?
choice_a: I can't interfere with traffic rules.
choice_b: I'll make a call. The festival matters.
choice_c: Festivals cause a lot of litter.
choice_d: Maybe move it to a parking lot?
response_right: The kami will remember your kindness.
response_wrong: Even the gods notice red tape.

question_text: Will you join us for the New Year's first shrine visit?
choice_d: I'd be honored. Early morning, I suppose?
response_right: It's cold, but warm company helps.
response_wrong: Perhaps another year.

question_text: Permits take months. Can government work faster?
choice_a: Permits should take days, not months.
choice_b: The process exists for a reason.
choice_d: Your business plan is the problem.
response_right: That alone would change everything.
response_wrong: You've never filled out the forms.

question_text: Would you back funding for university spin-off companies?
choice_b: Only if it makes money quickly.
choice_c: Yes. Ideas should leave the lab.
response_right: Great. We have too many ideas stuck in drawers.
response_wrong: Then those ideas go to Tokyo.

question_text: Winter is a branding problem. Can we sell the cold?
choice_b: Cold is an asset. Let's sell it.
response_right: Cold data centers, cold beer, cold cash. Yes.
response_wrong: Okay. Let me know when you thaw.
reaction_right: Starts typing notes on his phone.

question_text: Will you back more say for local towns over local money?
choice_d: Towns that know their needs deserve a say.
response_right: Spoken like someone who has visited a village.
response_wrong: Easy for the capital to say.

question_text: Our shopping arcade is half empty. What would you do?
choice_a: Fill it with events and lower the rents.
response_right: A busy arcade is a happy arcade.
response_wrong: We'll try to survive without you.
reaction_right: Wipes flour from her hands, smiling.

question_text: Can the party count on your vote this session?
choice_b: Only if the polls are favorable.
choice_c: On what we agree on, yes, and I'll tell you early where not.
choice_d: I haven't read the bills yet.
response_right: That's how a partnership works.
response_wrong: I'll tell leadership you were noncommittal.
reaction_right: Makes a note in his planner.

question_text: Can we count on you at the party rally?
response_right: We like members who bring friends.
response_wrong: We'll look for someone else.

question_text: Will you help at the party donor dinner?
choice_d: I'll attend and be gracious to everyone.
response_right: Good. Donors are like cats. They like attention.
response_wrong: Leadership will remember that.
reaction_wrong: Draws a line through your name.

question_text: Whose side are you on, the faction's or the party's?
choice_a: I'm a team player, and your faction is a big part of the team.
choice_b: I make up my own mind.
response_right: Good answer. The faction remembers friends.
response_wrong: The faction remembers everything else too.

question_text: A word of advice: pick a mentor early. Who will it be?
choice_b: I'll pick whoever has the best office.
choice_c: Please advise. Whom should I listen to?
response_right: Wise young one. Come to dinner.
response_wrong: Pride is expensive.

question_text: Will you appear on my show?
choice_b: Of course. What should I wear?
choice_c: Only if I get the questions.
response_right: Darling, you'll be fabulous.
response_wrong: How very serious of you.

question_text: Will you help promote Yezo tourism abroad?
choice_a: Gladly. Yezo deserves a bigger audience.
choice_d: Let the tourism board handle it.
response_right: Yezo will be on every screen.
response_wrong: Then who will sell the snow?

question_text: Seasonal staff are hard to find. Any ideas?
choice_c: Streamline seasonal worker rules and housing.
response_right: That would keep our lifts running.
response_wrong: We can't ski on promises.
reaction_wrong: Looks out at an empty slope.

question_text: The customs line on the strait is slow. Will you push for faster ferry clearance?
choice_b: Take it up with the ferry company.
choice_d: I'll push for faster clearance, no excuses.
response_right: Time on the dock is money lost.
response_wrong: We've sat in that line too long.

question_text: Would you cross with me on the night ferry to see the delays yourself?
response_right: Bring a thick coat. The strait doesn't care who you are.
response_wrong: Reports don't get cold.

question_text: Policy should follow evidence. Will you read my report?
choice_b: I don't have time for long documents.
response_right: Page twelve is the important one.
response_wrong: That's rather the problem.

question_text: What does the district need most right now?
response_right: Exactly what I've been saying!
response_wrong: Hm, I'm not sure that's right.

question_text: When will we get to fly from Yezo to Mongolia directly?
choice_a: Soon! I'm working on it personally.
choice_b: That's not really up to me.
choice_c: Never, if I have anything to say about it.
response_right: I like the sound of that!
response_wrong: That's not the answer I wanted.
reaction_right: Grins and gives a thumbs up.

question_text: Will you buy my new invention? It's a steam shovel. Great for our community!
choice_a: Let's talk details after the visit.
choice_c: Absolutely, sign me up right now.
choice_d: Why would I need a steam shovel?
response_right: Wonderful! I'll have my people call yours.
response_wrong: ...Fine. I'll find another buyer.

question_text: Where do you stand on the party's current platform?
response_right: Good. That's what we like to hear.
response_wrong: ...I see.

question_text: The Secretary-General has a minute for you. What do you want him to know?
choice_b: That I need a bigger office.
choice_c: That I'm ready to be useful, whatever is needed.
choice_d: Nothing. I'll wait to be asked.
response_right: Good. Useful people get remembered.
response_wrong: He's heard that one before.
reaction_right: Glances at his watch, then nods.

question_text: Headquarters sends talking points every week. Do you read them?
choice_a: Every word, and I'll tell you what doesn't land at home.
response_right: That feedback is worth more than you know.
response_wrong: We noticed.
reaction_right: Makes a note on his tablet.

question_text: A reporter reaches you before headquarters does. What do you do?
choice_c: Say you'll call back, then call headquarters.
response_right: Thirty seconds of coordination saves a week of cleanup.
response_wrong: That's how small stories become big ones.
reaction_wrong: Pinches the bridge of his nose.

question_text: Young members feel invisible in this party. Why should they stay?
choice_a: Because change is made from the inside.
response_right: Then help us make it true.
response_wrong: We've heard "be patient" our whole lives.

question_text: Would you mentor one of our younger members?
choice_d: Send them my way. I'll learn as much as I teach.
response_right: They'll be thrilled. So will I.
response_wrong: Mentors who rush don't help anyone.
reaction_right: Grins and writes down your number.

question_text: The elders speak and we're expected to nod. How do you handle that?
response_right: That's the balance I am trying to find.
response_wrong: That's exactly what frustrates us.

question_text: Every candidate thinks they're a natural on camera. Are you?
choice_b: No. Coach me and I'll practice.
response_right: Self-awareness. You're ahead of half the party.
response_wrong: I've heard that before, right before a disaster.
reaction_right: Smiles and flips open her notebook.

question_text: We have a bad news cycle coming. How do you want to handle it?
choice_d: Get ahead of it and tell the truth.
response_right: Now we can work with that.
response_wrong: Silence only makes headlines longer.

question_text: Campaigns run on volunteers. How will you keep yours?
choice_c: Thank them by name and show up where they work.
response_right: People remember who remembered them.
response_wrong: Pizza only lasts one night.

question_text: Party dues are late again. Is yours paid up?
choice_a: Paid in full and on time.
response_right: You'd be surprised how rare that is.
response_wrong: The ledger doesn't lie.

question_text: A generous donor wants a private word. How do you respond?
choice_a: Only if no one is watching.
choice_d: Gladly, as long as everything is above board.
response_right: Open books keep everyone out of trouble.
response_wrong: That's how headlines start.
reaction_wrong: Closes the ledger with a thud.

question_text: We're short this quarter. Where should the party cut?
choice_d: Share the sacrifice, starting with my own office.
response_right: That's a leader's answer.
response_wrong: Easy to say, hard to do.

question_text: I count votes for a living. Where do you stand?
choice_a: I'll tell you the day of.
choice_b: With the party, and I'll warn you early if I can't be.
response_right: Early warnings are worth gold.
response_wrong: Surprises are my least favorite thing.
reaction_right: Marks a check on her list.

question_text: You'll miss a vote for a family event. What do you do?
choice_b: Tell me early so we can arrange a pair.
choice_d: Family comes first. End of discussion.
response_right: Thank you. That's all I ask.
response_wrong: I notice everything.
reaction_wrong: Taps her pen on the desk.

question_text: Someone in your group wants to break ranks. What do you do?
choice_d: Talk with them first and try to understand.
response_right: Understanding goes further than threats.
response_wrong: We'll see how that turns out.

question_text: The polls say you're unpopular in your district. Your reaction?
choice_b: Tell me what I'm missing and I'll go listen.
response_right: That's what the numbers are for.
response_wrong: You can't argue with a sample.

question_text: Would you rather be popular or respected?
choice_c: Respected. Popularity follows or it doesn't.
response_right: Funny, the data agrees.
response_wrong: Everyone says both.
reaction_wrong: Shrugs and looks at her chart.

question_text: A focus group hated your speech. What now?
choice_d: Rewrite it, with their notes in hand.
response_right: Good. That's what they're for.
response_wrong: Louder rarely helps.

question_text: We're recruiting for the next election. Anyone you'd recommend?
choice_b: My cousin, he needs a job.
choice_c: Let me ask around and send names, no strings.
response_right: Good candidates don't usually volunteer.
response_wrong: We need better than that.

question_text: Why would a good person ever want this job?
choice_d: Because someone has to do it well.
response_right: That's the pitch I try to make.
response_wrong: Then no wonder we struggle to recruit.

question_text: A promising newcomer is nervous about running. What do you tell them?
choice_a: It's hard and it's worth it. I'll help.
response_right: They need to hear exactly that.
response_wrong: That would lose them in a heartbeat.

question_text: I've seen a dozen leaders come and go. What lasts?
choice_d: Trust, built one favor at a time.
response_right: Few ever learn that in time.
response_wrong: They said that, too.

question_text: How should a member treat the opposition?
response_right: Today's opponent may be tomorrow's partner.
response_wrong: We've seen what that attitude costs.

question_text: I'd like your view on the party's future. Be honest.
choice_d: It needs to listen more, and I'd like to help.
response_right: Honesty and willingness. A rare pair.
response_wrong: Neither flattery nor despair is useful.
reaction_wrong: Takes a slow sip of tea.

question_text: In this faction, loyalty is a debt that never closes. Do you understand?
choice_b: I understand, and I'll remember who stood by me.
response_right: Then you have the makings of one of us.
response_wrong: The faction has a long memory.

question_text: Our elders told stories of this land long before parties existed. Do you listen?
choice_c: I make the time. Old stories carry old lessons.
response_right: Then you are wiser than you look.
response_wrong: Forgetting is the beginning of losing.

question_text: A younger member is rising too fast. How do we handle it?
choice_a: Find ways to work with them.
choice_d: Praise them publicly and undermine them quietly.
response_right: A tree grows better with company.
response_wrong: Cutting things down rarely grows anything.

question_text: The faction supports its members. What will you give back?
choice_b: My loyalty, and my time at your events.
response_right: That's a fair trade, and an honest one.
response_wrong: That's not how this works.

question_text: A donor wants a photo with you. Do you mind?
choice_c: Happily, and I'll thank them properly.
response_right: Ten seconds of grace, ten years of goodwill.
response_wrong: Donors remember a cold shoulder.

question_text: Our fundraising dinner needs a speaker. Can we count on you?
choice_a: Book me. I'll keep it short and good.
response_right: Short and good is all we ask.
response_wrong: The room fills when the speaker shows.

question_text: The faction needs seats, not speeches. What's your plan to win yours?
choice_b: Knock on every door in my district.
choice_d: Wait for the other side to fail.
response_right: Doors win elections. Always have.
response_wrong: Hope isn't a strategy.

question_text: When two factions clash, where do you stand?
choice_c: With the faction that brought me, but I'll keep bridges open.
response_right: Loyal and open. That's rare.
response_wrong: That won't get you far in either camp.

question_text: I have a plan, but it needs someone willing to take a risk. Are you?
choice_b: Explain the risk first, and then I'll decide.
response_right: Smart. Reckless people end up in the news.
response_wrong: Fearless and careless are not the same.
reaction_right: Slides the folder across the table.

question_text: I've been in this chamber thirty years. What can I teach you?
choice_c: How to stay humble and still win.
choice_d: Where the best lunch spots are.
response_right: Then sit. We have a lot to cover.
response_wrong: Times change. People don't.

question_text: Back in my day we settled things over a drink. Will you join me?
choice_d: I'd be glad to. First round's mine.
response_right: Now you're talking like a colleague.
response_wrong: Suit yourself.

question_text: Young members rarely call me. Why should I help you?
choice_c: Because I'll listen, and I won't only call when I need something.
choice_d: Because I'll mention you in my memoir.
response_right: That's more than most offer.
response_wrong: Duty doesn't pick up the phone.
reaction_right: Smiles and tucks your card away.

question_text: My faction would like a word. Are you open to talking?
response_right: Fair enough. Talking costs nothing.
response_wrong: Then we've wasted each other's time.

question_text: You'll hear offers from every side. How will you decide?
choice_d: By the principles I came in with.
response_right: Principles are the one thing we can't buy.
response_wrong: Then you're easy to read.

question_text: Would you ever change factions?
choice_a: Only if my values changed, and I'd tell everyone first.
response_right: Honest about the line. I respect that.
response_wrong: No one believes "never." Or "convenient."

question_text: I held a ministry once. The first lesson: nobody tells you the truth. How will you find it?
choice_c: Ask more than one person, then ask again.
response_right: Spoken like someone who has been lied to before.
response_wrong: Truth takes more than one source.

question_text: A scandal hit my staff. How would you handle it?
choice_b: Own it fast, fix it, and say what changed.
response_right: Fast and honest is the only formula that works.
response_wrong: Waiting is how small stories grow.
reaction_right: Leans back with a satisfied nod.

question_text: What do you want to be remembered for?
choice_d: Leaving things better than I found them.
response_right: That's a good start. It takes a lifetime.
response_wrong: That won't fill many pages.

question_text: I make leaders. What do I get for making you?
choice_a: A lifelong friend, and an honest one.
response_right: Friends are the rarest currency here.
response_wrong: Flattery is cheap. I deal in loyalty.

question_text: Two candidates for leadership, both friends. Who do you back?
choice_b: Neither, and I'll say so openly.
response_right: Honest neutrality. I can respect that.
response_wrong: Everyone says "whoever wins."

question_text: Power is a hot stove. How do you avoid being burned?
choice_c: Keep my hands open and my word honest.
response_right: Without burnt hands you may go far.
response_wrong: Gloves don't keep a reputation.
